definition: A patch lies closer to A when its visible layout is dominated by long, straight, similarly oriented bands or boundaries. It lies closer to B when boundaries curve, change direction, or form a fragmented mosaic without one dominant orientation. Judge spatial organization rather than vegetation color or land-cover type.
cues: Long parallel edges or bands extending across much of the patch.
Elongated fields, planting rows, or woodland strips sharing a common orientation.
Straight, coherent major boundaries, including the shoreline in A5.
Toward B: irregular lake outlines, winding boundaries, and small parcels with varied orientations.
